newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish PM says he has backing for polls plan.
newsitem.headline: Turkish PM says he has backing for polls plan.

text.p: Turkey's Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Tuesday he had enough MPs behind him to win parliamentary backing for a plan to revamp his Islamist-led coalition and head for early elections.

"There is a majority in parliament. No once should have any worries about that," Erbakan told a meeting of his Welfare Party MPs. He did not refer to widespread speculation he would resign on Wednesday and hand over power to his secularist deputy.

A rightist Turkish leader with a key position in parliament said on Monday he would back Erbakan's plans to hand power to coalition ally Tansu Ciller and go to the polls to clear up a row with the army over Islamist activism.
On paper, the government is short of the majority it needs to get the power transfer and any election legislation through parliament.
But far-right powerbroker Muhsin Yazicioglu's eight MPs could help the coalition over parliamentary hurdles.
President Suleyman Demirel, an avowed secularist, must also approve the power handover. He has not given any indications if he will allow the plan to go ahead.
